headline: IAG CFO highlights strong underlying profit, lifted dividend franking, and upgraded FY27 margin and premium growth guidance despite headline profit decline
reasoning: William McDonnell clarified that the 25% headline profit decline was driven by non-recurring items in the prior year — specifically very benign natural perils and a business interruption provision release — rather than any deterioration in the underlying business. Underlying insurance profit grew marginally to $1.6 billion with a margin of around 15%. IAG has upgraded its FY27 guidance to gross written premium growth of 5–8% and reported insurance margins of 14.5–16.5%. The final dividend was lifted 5% to $0.20 per share, and the franking rate has increased to 80% with expectations of 80–100% going forward. Core retail brands delivered 7% growth in Q4, and the RACQ acquisition adds roughly one percentage point to FY27 growth.
quote: Actually our underlying profit is up. The the headline profit down only because last year we had really bumper year because there was very benign natural perils. And we had a release from a historical business interruption interruption provision when a case class action resolved. But actually the underlying profit is strong. And we're really pleased to be able to deliver this in a year where there were more natural perils. So we're a margin of around 15% and really importantly, also growth. So we had strong growth this year. And you may have seen we have strong growth guidance going forward. And we've lifted our margin guidance into next year. And the other thing I know you touched on was the dividend. We were pleased to lift the final dividend by 5% to $0.20 a share. And really importantly also the franking rate has lifted right up to 80%. And we expect that to be 80 to 100 going forward.
episode_title: IAG weathers the storm and upgrades its outlook

headline: IAG upgrades outlook, targeting 15%+ insurance margin and 15%+ ROE by FY27 on the back of AI-driven cost efficiencies
reasoning: IAG has lifted its guidance range with the midpoint above 15% insurance margin, which management describes as among the best for insurers globally. Admin costs are tracking below 11% for FY27, with the second half already 100 basis points lower than the prior period. AI and technology investments are credited as a key driver of these efficiencies, and importantly the investment is fully budgeted within the improving cost base. The FY27 guidance implies ROE of at least 15% and high single-digit EPS growth, which management believes positions IAG for top-quartile shareholder returns. IAG has also announced a partnership with OpenAI to develop next-generation AI applications for customer service and surge demand management.
quote: We said we want to be delivering a margin of above 15%. And the midpoint of our lifted guidance range is is above 15%. We want it to lean more into growth. And you can we've talked about that increased growth ambition that we have. And even in the guidance for FY 27, what those will do is give us an ROE of at least 15%, which is among the best of insurers in the world and high single digit EPs growth. And we think that's going to help us deliver for shareholders top quartile shareholder returns.
episode_title: IAG weathers the storm and upgrades its outlook
